rules.rule: a download of an electron-updater feed with no sha512, or a package of RELEASES with no SHA1
an appcast enclosure with no EdDSA signature, or a Tauri platform with no signature
a feed or an entry of it that names no file to download
an absolute address of a download or of release notes that is not https
a download on another host than the first download of the same feed
a version that the updater cannot read or compare
an appcast whose first item is not the one with the highest sparkle:version
the same version in two entries of one feed
a version that is equal to or lower than the one of the previous feed
a file the feed offers that is not in the dist folder
a size or length in the feed that differs from the file in the dist folder
a checksum in the feed that differs from the one of the file in the dist folder
a Tauri feed without one of windows-x86_64, darwin-x86_64, darwin-aarch64 and linux-x86_64, or a folder without one of latest.yml, latest-mac.yml and latest-linux.yml
a rollout value that the updater cannot use
an electron-updater feed whose version is lower than another feed of the same channel in the folder
an update with no release notes in the feed
a feed file that the tool could not read as its kind
a folder or a set of inputs past a limit of the run

findings.found: the first item has sparkle:version 412, but the item at line 16 has 420, which is higher; put the newest item first
findings.fix: put the items in order, newest first, as generate_appcast writes them

basis.text: an appcast item has sparkle:version, the version the machine compares, sparkle:shortVersionString for people, and an enclosure with the url, length and type of the archive

findings.own: the tool's own choice: the first item of an appcast must have the highest sparkle:version; Sparkle picks the best item itself, but people, other tools and scripts that read the appcast take the first item as the newest

findings.found: the download "http://downloads.quillmere.test/clip/QuillmereClip-4.1.2.zip" uses http, not https, so it can be read or changed on the way
findings.fix: serve the file over https and write the https address in the feed

basis.text: the updater enforces TLS in production unless a setting lets it accept endpoints that are not HTTPS
an app keeps its EdDSA public key in SUPublicEDKey, every update is signed with the private key, and updates should be served over HTTPS
basis.source: Documentation, basic setup and EdDSA signatures (Sparkle)

findings.own: every absolute address of a download, a release notes link or a package of RELEASES whose scheme is not https; an address with no scheme is relative to the feed and is served the way the feed is; namespace declarations of XML are not addresses and are not read

findings.found: the item of version 420 has sparkle:phasedRolloutInterval but no pubDate, which Sparkle needs to place the groups of a phased rollout
findings.fix: write the share as a number from 0 to 100 (a percentage for Squirrel.Windows, with # right after the size), and give a phased Sparkle item its pubDate

basis.text: a staged rollout is set by hand with stagingPercentage in the update info file, a number from 0 to 100 that is the share of users who get the version
sparkle:phasedRolloutInterval gives the number of seconds between seven groups of users, and the item must then have a pubDate
a staged rollout adds # and a percentage after the size, with no space before # for clients older than 1.4.0, and a pulled version must be followed by a higher one

findings.own: a stagingPercentage that is not a number from 0 to 100, a sparkle:phasedRolloutInterval that is not a whole number of seconds above 0 or that has no pubDate in its item, and a "# nn%" of RELEASES that is not from 0% to 100% or has a space before #

findings.found: the enclosure of version 400 has no sparkle:edSignature, only the deprecated sparkle:dsaSignature
findings.fix: sign the archive with the private key of the app (generate_appcast for Sparkle, the signer of the Tauri CLI) and put the signature itself in the feed

basis.text: DSA signatures are deprecated and kept only for the move to EdDSA; after it, every update in the appcast carries its sparkle:edSignature
an app keeps its EdDSA public key in SUPublicEDKey, every update is signed with the private key, and updates should be served over HTTPS
basis.source: Documentation, basic setup and EdDSA signatures (Sparkle)

basis.text: the signature is the content of the .sig file of the build; a path or a URL in its place does not work

findings.own: an enclosure of an appcast, delta enclosures too, with no sparkle:edSignature or one that is not the base64 of 64 bytes, and a Tauri platform with no signature or with a path or address in its place; the tool cannot check a signature against the public key of the app
